title: Rule 54 shows only repetitive or nested forms in 100 million initial conditions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rule 54 shows only repetitive or nested forms in 100 million initial conditions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Rule 54, a possible class 4 elementary cellular automaton, shows only repetitive or nested behavior in its first hundred million initial conditions, leaving it uncertain whether rule 54 is universal.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And as one continues one sees various other repetitive and nested forms. But at least up to the hundred millionth initial condition one sees nothing that is fundamentally any more complicated.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “The Threshold of Universality in Cellular Automata” (from p. 694), p. 697. Scope: the rule 54 elementary cellular automaton

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-21: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The finite rule and initial-condition range can be regenerated with standard computation. Some interpretation is required, but the bounded historical observation is reproducible rather than a claim about all time.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the stated enumeration order, evolve rule 54 from each of the first 100 million finite initial conditions to a prespecified horizon, and classify each trace using explicit periodicity and nesting tests. One certified counterexample refutes the observation; exhaustive agreement confirms it only for the chosen horizon and definitions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fundamental complexity and nesting require operational definitions.

The simulation horizon is not stated.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a finite census, not an assertion that rule 54 is simple for every seed. Regenerating a hundred million short evolutions is ordinary computation, and the book already supplies formulas for the patterns it highlights. The judgment more complicated must be frozen into a classifier, but once that is done the census can confirm or refute the stated bound.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate rule 54's initial conditions in the book's order through the hundred millionth, run each to a pre-set horizon, and classify the evolution as periodic, nested with an explicit formula, or neither. Finding one evolution that is neither refutes the report; agreement through the whole range confirms it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fundamentally more complicated has to be replaced by a mechanical classifier before two reruns must agree.

A finite time cutoff can mistake a long transient for nesting, or miss structure that appears later.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Rule 54, run from each of the first N initial conditions (binary digits of n on a white background, as in NKS p. 697), produces only repetitive or nested patterns: none has the local space-time complexity characteristic of class 3 or class 4 behaviour.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py evolves rule 54 for 256 steps from every initial condition n = 1..65535 (binary digits of n on white; batches of 512 vectorised in numpy on a lattice wide enough that the light cone never reaches the edge), encodes every 6 x 6 space-time tile with top-left in rows 128..250 inside the light cone as a 36-bit integer and counts distinct tiles D; patterns with D <= 400 are also tested for exact temporal periodicity (period <= 16) of the light-cone core over steps 128..256. The 20 initial conditions with the largest D are re-run for 512 steps. Per-initial-condition values in derived/census.csv.xz; runtime about 3 minutes.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Family: initial conditions n = 1..65536 (16 bits), cell values = binary digits of n placed on an infinite white background (validated against the figure: n = 1 single cell, n = 3 two cells, n = 291 nested); rule 54 run for T = 256 steps on a lattice wide enough that the light cone never reaches the edge. Classifier (frozen before the census): the number D of distinct 6 x 6 space-time tiles whose top-left corner lies in rows 128..250 and inside the light cone (plus 2 cells) of the pattern. Calibration on controls outside the family, disclosed: repetitive and nested rules give D <= 1007 (rule 90 single cell 115, random 14-bit seeds 267-395; rule 150 single 316, random seeds 804-1007; rule 22 single 119; rule 18 random 309-602; rules 250, 108, 184, 62, 41 random 1-178), while class 3/4 controls give D >= 1094 (rule 110 random 14- and 30-bit seeds 1094-1553; rule 30 6801-7166; rule 45 6338-6401), with a few class-3 rules from narrow seeds in between (rule 106: 462 and 2912; rule 126: 130-402; rule 146: 371-413; rule 73: 64-774). The eight rule-54 patterns shown in the book's figure (n = 1, 3, 75, 259, 291, 787, 803, 56549) give D = 10, 37, 315, 315, 286, 391, 391, 370, and a batch of 256 random 14-bit seeds gave max 391. Threshold: D > 1050 (geometric midpoint of 1007 and 1094) = 'more complicated'. Also recorded per initial condition: exact temporal periodicity (period <= 16) of the pattern's core over steps 128..256 ('repetitive'). The claim PASSES if 0 of the 65536 initial conditions has D > 1050. Reported, not decisive: the distribution of D, the fraction that is exactly periodic, the number with D > 700 (a stricter threshold that still clears all rule-54 book examples), and for any initial condition above threshold a re-run with T = 512.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. The claim FAILS if at least one initial condition n <= 65536 has D > 1050 and the T = 512 re-run also gives D > 1050 (sustained local complexity comparable to the class 3/4 controls). If some exceed 1050 at T = 256 but not at T = 512 the verdict is 'mixed' (transient complexity). The census is 1/1526 of the book's 10^8 initial conditions; a pass is consistent with the claim but far from exhausting it.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: number of initial conditions n <= 65536 whose rule-54 pattern has more than 1050 distinct 6x6 tiles in steps 128-256

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: exhaustive over n = 1..65535 (n = 65536 has 17 bits and was not included)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: The claim is a finite observational statement about the first 10^8 initial conditions; the full census is beyond a few minutes of Python, so this is a scaled census (2^16 initial conditions) with the book's informal judgement 'nothing fundamentally more complicated than repetitive or nested' frozen into a local-complexity classifier. The classifier counts distinct 6 x 6 space-time tiles in the second half of the evolution: self-similar (nested) and periodic patterns have bounded tile vocabularies, whereas class 3 patterns have thousands and class 4 patterns with interacting gliders over a thousand. The threshold was set from controls outside the rule-54 family plus the book's own eight rule-54 examples; it is admittedly coarse, and the random-seed rule 150 controls (nested, up to 1007) show that nested patterns with wide seeds approach it. A failure under this classifier would therefore need the T = 512 confirmation and visual inspection before being read as a counterexample to Wolfram's census.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Rule 54 from initial conditions 1..65536 (generated by analysis.py)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Pre-registered decision: 0 of 65,535 initial conditions exceeds the 1050-tile threshold (0 exceed even the stricter 700). The largest vocabulary is 426 tiles (n = 52843) and the twenty largest all fall back to 391 tiles at steps 256-512, the same vocabulary as the book's examples n = 787 and 803; the distribution is strongly clustered (median 68; 50,561 below 100; 214 between 400 and 500), consistent with a small repertoire of repetitive and nested forms. 17.2% of the patterns are exactly periodic in the core with period 4 over steps 128-256.

This is a scaled census: 2^16 initial conditions rather than the 10^8 of the book, i.e. seeds of at most 16 cells, so wider seeds (where interacting structures are more likely) are untested; a pass here is consistent with Wolfram's census but does not reproduce it.

'Repetitive or nested' was frozen into a local-complexity classifier (distinct 6 x 6 space-time tiles) with a threshold set from controls outside the family (rule 90/150/22/18 nested, rules 250/108/184/62/41 repetitive, rules 110/30/45 complex) and the book's own eight rule-54 examples. The margin is large (426 observed vs. 1094 for the least complex rule-110 control) but the classifier is coarse: a class-4-like pattern with a small glider repertoire could in principle have a modest tile vocabulary, and nested patterns from wide seeds (rule 150 random 14-bit seeds reach 1007) approach the threshold.

Finite horizon (256 steps, re-checks to 512): slowly developing complexity, e.g. structures appearing only after thousands of steps, would be missed.
